To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the click probability distribution of search engines’ results pages obeys a new function, the SPM function, which is a generalization of the Zipf function, 2) the SPM function is a function of two parameters, the first one is the same as that of Zipf function, the second one represents the Serial Position Effect, 3) the Serial Position Effect is a function of the position of an entry in the result page, 4) the SPM functions
the click probability distribution of search engines’ entries on result pages can be described by the new function we propose, which is the product of two factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the click probability distribution of the entries of search result pages?
how users interact with the results of search engine queries, and the factors that affect the users’ click behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the click behavior of search engines’ users is affected by both the Zipf distribution and Serial Position Effects.
the click probability distribution of search results does not obey the monotonic decreasing Zipfs law, but instead is the joint result of the Zipf law and Serial Position Effects.
the click probability distribution is a combination of the two functions, i.e. Zipf function and our new function, with the former dominating the latter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the click probability distribution is a function of both the Zipf distribution and the Serial Position Effects.
we have found that the Serial Position Effects are not negligible and should be considered when designing search engines and analyzing search engine logs.
we provide a new way of thinking about the click behavior of users on the result pages of search engines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the click probability distribution of the search engine entries is a function of the serial position of the entry on the result page, and the click probability distribution on the result page is independent of the order in which the search engine returns the results.
, the click probability of a search result can be affected not only by its ranking, but also by its serial position in the result list.
the click probability distribution of search engine result pages is influenced not only by the ranking of search results, but also by the presentation of search result pages.
